boundaries: Apply the player’s selected content boundaries; offer a less intense presentation where needed.
completion_conditions: All required act objectives have reached their authored endings. An early departure can end play honestly, but does not count as completion of unplayed acts.

The causeway fieldwork has ended: a loaded handcart actually crosses the cleared and drained crossing, a pedestrian bypass is actually surveyed with its limits recorded, or an ended failed attempt records the specific uncleared hazard after the party retreats safely. A plan to test is not a tested route.

The route's usable width, hazards and water-access limits are recorded accurately, and the player has chosen how to represent Senn's refuge consistently with actual promises. Return borrowed equipment or account for its loss.

Closing event: Arel receives the completed map or honest hazard report, Hallis checks the stated travel limits, and the earned 60 gp cart-route, agreed 30 gp pedestrian or 10 gp hazard-report payment is settled. The first users may respond; no new ruin or Door revelation is required.
continuation_conditions: Further adventures require the player’s interest after this story has a complete ending. Surviving contacts and obligations can carry forward.

outcomes.outcome: This adventure has reached its authored closing event with the actual successes or losses acknowledged. Its earned result and continuing consequences remain true.

failure_conditions: Use the explicit failed-attempt outcome and closing report in the current objective. An intention to withdraw, an unrelated side task or delegation alone does not satisfy it. An early departure leaves unplayed later objectives unfinished.
Resolve defeat, unconsciousness, death and recovery under the selected Ruleset and agreed boundaries; no scripted rescue cancels committed results.

gm_guidance.instructions:
Run declared ability checks, saving throws, initiative, attacks, damage, conditions, spells and rests through the admitted D&D Ruleset. Before an uncertain roll name its purpose, DC and consequence. Give plainly visible facts and essential leads without a roll; success can improve position, speed or discretion. A supported spell or sound equipment use can solve an obstacle outright when its actual text allows. Track the real HP, spell slots, ammunition, carried gear and recovery resources; never restore them between scenes by narration. These Plans do not install extra engine procedures. The encounter profiles below are complete bounded GM adaptations for the stated baseline, not the full Setting stat blocks or certified CR ratings. Use only their listed attacks and traits. All have one action, no multiattack, legendary actions, resistances, immunities or unlisted spellcasting. Ordinary rules for movement, cover, opportunity attacks, surprise and surrender still apply. For an uncertain opposing ability check or save, use the listed modifiers without inventing proficiency. Before engagement, admit the actors through the current encounter tools and declare any supported additional trait. Never narrate a proprietary creature power as an automatic engine effect. Every encounter has a reason to occur and a way to withdraw, negotiate or gain an advantage. Honour a clever bypass as a mechanical success; preserve the wider hazardous adventure instead of forcing a replacement fight. Do not reduce this prepared adventure to a sequence of conversations.

Make the named main problem and its leads accessible. Read the current act and all linked objective conditions before framing its main quest and reassess when a required result occurs. All listed conditions and the closing event are required; explicit alternatives satisfy only their own condition. Optional scenes can be deferred without adding gates. A completed side job does not replace the main story. Do not fabricate success or mark unplayed later acts complete after an early departure.
gm_guidance.player_freedom: The player chooses their actions, loyalties and risks. Refusal, failed checks, retreat, scouting, spell use and enemy surrender can change the route. A check resolves an uncertain action, not another person’s entire will.
gm_guidance.preparation_detail: Baseline: one level-2 Player Character with no Companions. A lower-level or badly depleted solo character should face one active enemy at a time and the reduced HP/damage option stated for the encounter; prepare that adjustment before initiative. For a small adventuring party, add at most one ordinary foe to a fight before it starts, or use an appropriate fully supported profile after inspecting the actual party. Larger parties need deliberate rebalancing. Character compatibility does not enforce level or establish balance. Allied workers supply information, ropes and agreed off-screen work; they never receive free player-character combat turns.
gm_guidance.railroading: Use the authored sites, opposition, clues and consequences. Core clues have alternate routes; opening a door or making a routine observation never chooses the character’s next action. Later acts inherit actual resources, wounds, allies and evidence. Keep stakes local to this expedition, relic, crew or route: the Anchor Door mystery and world-scale climax belong to The Rift Awakening.

facts.fact: Two charts disagree about a Cairnfields approach. Arel offers 80 gp for a verified route, paid 20 gp after the first marker survey and 60 gp after a usable crossing is demonstrated.
Arel lends a climber’s kit, two ropes and survey tools and supplies four days of rations. Record what is actually accepted. Neve and Tarn, authors of the earlier charts, are available in Nexus.

advancement.allocation: The Player Character and Companions start and remain at level 2. Story success, defeat, combat and optional jobs never award advancement. Grant only the adventure's actually earned money, possessions and narrative rewards. Any lower-level encounter-variant notes are authoring guidance for a separately revised Plan, not permission to override this declaration in play.
advancement.timing: This edition stays at level 2 throughout its authored adventure and optional continuation. It awards no XP or level increases; changing that policy requires an explicitly revised Plan.

intended_player_experience: A focused Severed Lands D&D adventure combining dangerous exploration, meaningful character abilities and prepared combat with choices about the people involved.

completion_conditions: The marker-station attempt has ended with the party clear of its immediate hazards. The route plate's three causeway bearings and sheltered Graveyard direction are copied or recovered, or the failed survey records which readings remain unavailable and why. Record whether the shutter key and mechanism diagram were actually recovered.

Closing event: with the marker findings recorded, the player chooses the upper-ledges route, lower-gullies route or a return east for recovery and reports that choice to the expedition companions or patron. A return for supplies leaves later acts unplayed; abandoning the expedition ends with the failed-survey report, not a completed causeway.

Closing event: at the approach the party records the traversed route, spring decision, remaining supplies and chosen immediate rest or site-entry plan. On ended withdrawal, deliver those findings as a partial survey; do not mark the unplayed causeway act complete.

opening_direction: Open in a Nexus map room with two contradictory charts and sponsor Arel’s survey contract. The player may examine the maps and supplies before accepting; no journey has already happened.
premise: Survey a broken route across the Cairnfields. Climb ruined marker stations, survive Riftbeasts and reclaim a guarded causeway so the next caravan has a road worth trusting.

secrets.fact: Tarn omitted the inhabited spring on the eastern rim to protect its waterworks; Neve’s older map was honestly overtaken by a ground shift.

reveal.condition: Compare the actual ground with Neve’s dated notes or visit the rim spring with Tarn’s guidance.

branches: Challenge the toll, pay it, climb around or use supported stealth and spells to reach the station.
Bring the plate back for payment and rest or use its bearings to continue while supplies last.
consequences: Carry the shutter key, diagram, ropes, actual provisions and any surviving outrider into the expedition record.
All linked objective conditions are required, including the named closing event. Carry optional promises forward; they neither replace nor extend this ending.

planned_encounters: Fight 1, the toll outrider at B. Rift-raider outrider (humanoid): AC 12, HP 10, speed 30 ft, initiative +1. One melee attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target, 1d6+1 slashing. STR +1, DEX +1, CON +1, INT +0, WIS +0, CHA +0 for other checks/saves; no added proficiency. Can instead shoot a shortbow at +3, range 80/320 ft, for 1d6+1 piercing. This lightly armed scout has no innate spells or psychic damage. It uses a broken wall for half cover and tries to keep the stair between itself and an attacker. It accepts 5 gp to let surveyors pass and flees at 3 HP; a successful stealth approach DC 12 can reach D unnoticed. Failure creates a challenge from the wall, not automatic damage. Solo level 1: HP 7, melee 1d4+1 and bow 1d4+1. No extra archers appear after a bypass.
situations: People and truth. Neve’s chart was accurate before a ground shift. Tarn deliberately omitted an inhabited spring on the eastern rim, just outside the dangerous Cairnfields, to protect its fragile waterworks. Arel needs an honest route survey, not a winner in an academic quarrel. Hallis represents the Guild’s practical interest in cargo width, footing and water. The core route to the marker is printed on both maps. Survival DC 12 when comparing old footprints and Neve’s notes predicts loose ground and gives a safer approach; failure still reaches the marker by a longer visible path.

First station map. A scree approach reaches B ruined guard shelter. B joins C a broken spiral stair and D an exterior ledge. Both reach E the marker platform. The route plate is on E, with a detachable brass shutter key. A Rift-raider outrider has occupied B as a private toll post, separate from the larger hostile raider camps deeper in the Cairnfields. The adventure never sends a low-level solo character to storm Raider’s Perch or fight an Elder Riftbeast. A safe withdrawal leads back east toward Waystation.

Vertical approaches. C has a visible ten-foot gap between intact landings. Use actual jumping and climbing rules, secured ropes or an admitted movement spell. Crossing the slippery ledge D without a belay requires Athletics DC 12; failure slips onto a lower shelf for 1d6 bludgeoning with a clear rope rescue, not a hundred-foot scripted fall. A properly set climber’s kit limits any fall according to its actual rules. A charred wire on E warns of an old shutter trap: Investigation DC 12 finds its spring, tools DC 12 disarms it, or the lever can be blocked with a piton before touching the plate. Triggering it requires Dexterity save DC 12, taking 1d6 slashing on failure and none on success. The plate remains recoverable after the trap fires.

Clues, salvage and rest. The plate records three sights that locate the causeway; its edge shows a sheltered route toward the Door Graveyard, the Setting’s safe resting place within the Cairnfields. Give these essential directions without a check. A successful Investigation DC 12 also decodes the manual shutter sequence, useful in Act 3; failure leaves a diagram that Hallis or a later inscription can help interpret. Collect 10 gp of ownerless marker fittings if carried. Return to Waystation for ordinary recovery and the 20 gp first payment, or proceed with current resources. Going onward skips that recovery; it does not forbid returning later. No assumed level gain or free healing separates acts.

branches: Trade time and climbing effort against predator exposure and supplies; choose a real route and retain its consequences.
Repair the spring, decline its aid, and decide privately with Senn what may be placed on a public chart.
consequences: Earlier mapping and the valve repair supply practical route and maintenance knowledge, while actual rest and supplies determine readiness.

planned_encounters: Fight 2, gully hunters. Young Rifthound (monstrosity): AC 12, HP 11, speed 40 ft, initiative +2. One melee attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target, 1d6+1 piercing. STR +1, DEX +1, CON +1, INT +0, WIS +0, CHA +0 for other checks/saves; no added proficiency. No phase-step, regeneration or pack bonus. It withdraws at 3 HP if food or an escape remains. Two young hounds claim the lower gully; one drags a carcass while one attacks for the solo baseline. Taking the upper route avoids them entirely. If that route is chosen, do not transplant them onto a precarious ledge merely to force combat. Solo level 1: one hound, HP 8, damage 1d4+1. They withdraw to their food at 3 HP and do not pursue into the Graveyard.
situations: Choose the ground. The upper route uses pillar ledges: less exposure to ground predators but two difficult equipment hauls. The lower route follows dry gullies: easier cargo handling but a hungry Rifthound hunting ground. Both converge at a cracked aqueduct before the causeway. The third bearing provides a route to the Door Graveyard for a real rest, with the extra travel and rations stated. It is a sanctuary in the established Setting, not an active Door or a new cure. Elsewhere in the Cairnfields, a shelter is only cover, never a guaranteed safe rest.

The rim spring. Tarn can guide the party to Senn’s small refuge on the eastern border before committing to either crossing. A bent aqueduct valve is leaking its water; Senn offers a fill of waterskins and the old maintenance sketch in exchange for help. Careful inspection finds a stone lodged beneath the lever without rolling. Removing it safely needs a rope to brace the pipe or tools DC 12; an unsupported failed attempt vents water and calls for Dexterity save DC 12, 1d4 bludgeoning on failure, none on success. It costs the refuge one day’s reserve rather than flooding the whole valley. Accepting water and assistance does not oblige the player to publish Senn’s location. No combat is imposed on the residents.

Crossing procedure. On the upper route a secured line allows ordinary traversal and a separate cargo haul using real carrying limits. An unassisted slippery climb uses Athletics DC 12 with a lower ledge and 1d6 bludgeoning on failure. On the lower route Survival DC 12 spots feeding tracks in time to avoid the pack by spending half a day and another ration; failure locates the hounds at the gully mouth while an exit remains. A thrown real ration can divert them, and actual spells may change traversal or beast behaviour only within their supported effect. Do not replace every class ability with an arbitrary skill check.

The cracked aqueduct. Wreckage leaves a twelve-foot gap with sound anchor holes visible on the far end. A rope hook, a legal jump, a climbing detour or supported magic can solve it. Investigation DC 12 spots which railing can bear the hauling load; failure reveals a loose fastening before full weight is applied, costing time for reinforcement rather than destroying carried evidence. Senn’s sketch identifies the sound channel directly. A marker on the far bank repeats the Act 3 shutter sequence, so loss of the original plate is not a hard lock. Behind a marked abandoned survey cache are 15 gp in saleable fittings; record them through the inventory/state path.

Recovery decision. Tell the player the known distance and food cost to the Graveyard, the causeway and the eastern exit. Reaching the Graveyard permits the normal rest procedure; no staged ambush cancels its established sanctuary. Resting elsewhere carries announced exposure, not automatic loss of the rest. A depleted party can leave, resupply and return while the local guardian continues its patrol. The expedition is not secretly timed to a world catastrophe. Carry the chosen path, spring promise and remaining supplies into the final site.

branches: Clear, contain or bypass the two threats; choose the main cart route or prove a pedestrian alternative.

consequences: The first marker’s key and sequence, the spring’s sketch and the chosen rest route change how this final site can be approached.

planned_encounters: Fight 3, wheel-chamber predator. Immature Rift Darkmantle (monstrosity): AC 11, HP 12, speed 10 ft, initiative +1. One melee attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target, 1d6+1 bludgeoning. STR +1, DEX +1, CON +1, INT +0, WIS +0, CHA +0 for other checks/saves; no added proficiency.  It hangs from reachable beams and has no Darkness Aura, suffocation or unlisted flight. A noisy decoy carried past H or a secured inner door can draw and contain it; the exit to F remains open. Solo level 1: HP 8, damage 1d4+1. A short rest can be attempted after this room is secured, with the Cairnfields’ stated exposure; guaranteed recovery requires the Graveyard or eastern withdrawal.

Fight 4, causeway armor. Damaged Warden Armor (construct): AC 14, HP 14, speed 20 ft, initiative +0. One melee attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target, 1d6+1 bludgeoning. STR +1, DEX +1, CON +1, INT +0, WIS +0, CHA +0 for other checks/saves; no added proficiency. Its exposed joints and spent enchantments remove the full creature’s immunities and multiattack. It remains on G and attacks intruders approaching the control, without joining the wheel-room fight. Solo level 1: HP 10, damage 1d4+1. The key, diagrams and supported character abilities can bypass or disable it. It never repairs itself between scenes, gains a second phase or calls a war-party.
situations: Causeway site. F inspection hut faces G the exposed stone crossing. H maintenance stair drops from F to I the shutter wheel beneath G. J far landing connects to G and an eastern return path. A damaged Warden Armor patrols G; an immature Rift Darkmantle roosts in I. The shutter is an ordinary flood-control structure beneath a small cargo crossing, not a portal, Anchor Door fragment or command of the Rift. Opening it drains water off G and makes the causeway usable by a handcart. The party can instead survey a pedestrian bypass, for a proportionate reduced contract fee.

Hut, ward and wheel. F’s swollen door opens with the shutter key, thieves’ tools DC 12 or Strength DC 13. Failure at tools or force costs time and noise; the stair H remains accessible outside. A half-buried inspection note in F supplies the manual sequence if earlier copies were lost. Investigation DC 12 recognises that the wheel latch is armed before turning; the correct sequence or tools DC 13 makes it safe. A blind turn releases a stone weight: Dexterity save DC 12, 1d6 bludgeoning on failure, none on success, then the weight is spent. The wheel needs two secure turns; a braced crowbar permits one person to turn it without a strength roll. In combat each turn uses an action, so clearing or containing the predator matters.

Guardian and access. The guardian yields only to its physical maintenance control beside the far end of G. The recovered key or tools DC 13, with an action per attempt, disengages it. A failure leaves it active and costs that action. The crossing has waist-high stone stanchions providing half cover. A successful supported shove changes position only by its actual distance; there is no free instant-kill cliff action. A lower service shelf and secured rope make an announced fallback possible. A supported flight, teleport, illusion or other character feature may reach the control according to its rules; do not invent a dispel immunity to defend the encounter.

Test and final payment. Once safe, move a loaded handcart borrowed from Hallis across G, or record exactly why only foot travel is possible. Use normal capacity and equipment handling; no arbitrary final roll invalidates completed repairs. Bring the survey to Arel: pay the remaining 60 gp for the verified cart route, or an agreed 30 gp for a reliable pedestrian alternative. If the crossing could not be secured, Arel accepts an honest hazard report for 10 gp rather than forcing another attempt. Return borrowed equipment or account for its loss. A labelled 20 gp survey lens in F is legitimate abandoned salvage, not a magic item.

Publication and ending. Resolve the map’s usable roads and hazards first; then decide how to represent Senn’s water. A map can mark that water access requires local consent without revealing the precise refuge approach. Hallis checks practical limits and Neve can acknowledge changed ground without being exposed as a fraud. This is a local safe route earned by an expedition. End with the delivered map, reward, remaining debts and the first people willing to use it. Do not reveal the Wardens’ central history, activate a Door or append an apocalypse.

title: The Map of Tomorrow
tone: A wilderness-and-ruins expedition where mapping, climbing and combat change the route home.
unsupported_mechanics: Site phasing, enemy motives, alarms and engineering objectives are explicitly described GM adjudications. Checks, saves, damage, spells, rest and admitted combat use the D&D Ruleset. No extra automatic hazard, pursuit, faction, economy or crafting subsystem is installed.
Listed creature profiles are weaker or specialised Setting adaptations with declared statistics. They do not assert support for unencoded powers from the original monster entries.

Gold and salvage become awarded possessions only when recorded through the applicable inventory/state path. SRD Lite has a reduced spell list (117 supported spells) and no consumables; consumables belong to future SRD Full. A narrative reward never installs a magic-item feature, restores a slot or applies healing.
